PullRequest.Title: sessions: include associated PRs in archive nudge
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

The Agents Window archive nudge previously considered only PR artifacts, missing PRs associated through Create PR or explicit selection.

- Combine artifacts with session-owned GitHub PR references across workspace folders, normalizing and deduplicating identities.
- Share provider-neutral ownership filtering with the session hover; exclude inherited checkout PRs and preserve legacy primary-PR handling.
- Keep the safety checks: every distinct qualifying PR must resolve as merged through the shared live GitHub model, and invalid GitHub input still blocks the nudge.
- Update localized setting/accessibility help wording and telemetry count classifications; add focused nudge, ownership, and provider regression tests.

Targets `release/1.138` with a single fix commit. Enterprise-host support remains unchanged and is intentionally out of scope. No new UI surface or telemetry fields.

## Validation

- 35 focused Electron unit tests passed: archive nudge, shared ownership helper, and provider baseline/Create PR/explicit-selection associations.
- `npm run transpile-client` passed.
- `node_modules\.bin\tsc.cmd --project build\checker\tsconfig.browser.json --pretty false` passed.
- `npm run precommit` passed hygiene checks for all 8 changed files.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Unit test command:

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\chat\test\browser\sessionArchiveNudge.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\services\sessions\test\common\session.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --grep "SessionArchiveNudge|getSessionOwnedGitHubPullRequestRefs|filters folder-session baseline pull requests|publishes Create PR and explicit selection associations"
```

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an eligible inactive session and evaluate whether to show the archive nudge for artifact and session-owned associated pull requests.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The nudge cannot appear until every distinct qualifying PR has a live GitHubPullRequestModel state of merged. On a cold model, refresh completion is on this critical path; with an already-populated shared model, the current state is immediately readable and the triggered refresh proceeds asynchronously.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh pull-request details and reviews through GitHubPullRequestModel; each distinct cold PR model issues one PR request and one reviews request, then polling may repeat every 60 seconds while a polling client remains.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two concurrent HTTP requests per distinct qualifying PR on an uncached refresh; duplicate artifact/association identities and overlapping consumers coalesce. Agent-host association history is capped at 10 per folder, while additional workspace folders contribute only their distinct identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The nudge created/refreshed models only for qualifying PR artifacts and did nothing for association-only PRs. Other GitHub contributions already acquire and poll first-folder session PR models, so for the common active-session path the newly included identities generally reuse/coalesce with existing model work; distinct association-only identities from otherwise-untracked folders are newly reached by the nudge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold live PR state must arrive before the nudge can establish that all PRs are merged. Subsequent polling is off the immediate display computation but keeps state current.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct normalized owner/repo/number identities after deduplication across artifacts and workspace folders. Agent-host metadata retains at most 10 PR references per folder; artifacts and duplicate associations collapse to one model key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One shared model per normalized PR key. Each model coalesces overlapping refresh calls through _refreshPromise, and duplicate polling clients share one scheduler. Different PR models refresh concurrently; each refresh performs its two requests concurrently with Promise.all.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHubPullRequestModel references are shared by normalized key and retain ETags while referenced. Warm consumers reuse current observable state; overlapping refreshes coalesce. References and polling disposables are released when the reactive input changes, the session becomes ineligible/hidden, or the nudge is disposed. There is no negative cache for failed refreshes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the changed call path, per-key deduplication, two-request refresh boundary, 60-second polling, and shared-model coalescing; moderate confidence in incremental network magnitude because other active-session consumers usually own the same models.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Generic providers are not contractually capped by IGitHubInfo, and multi-root sessions can contribute references from multiple folders, but repository evidence does not establish realistically large qualifying sets. Existing active-session GitHub surfaces also already keep common first-folder models warm, making the incremental request count smaller than the raw association count in normal use.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff intentionally extends authoritative merged-state checks to association-only PRs, but identities are normalized/deduplicated, agent-host history is bounded, and shared models coalesce refresh and polling work. There is insufficient evidence of realistic cardinality or incremental fan-out severe enough to justify rolling back or redesigning the required live-state check.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render session hover pull-request links after extracting the shared ownership filter.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hover construction synchronously reads first-folder GitHub metadata, filters owned references, and maps them to display/link objects; no asynchronous work or boundary call is required by the changed helper.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of first-folder pull-request refs; agent-host producers cap this history at 10.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous local array filtering/mapping; no concurrency or queueing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is introduced or bypassed. The helper returns a filtered array when provenance is present, matching the previous inline filter, and falls back to the legacy primary ref as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the direct before/after comparison in sessionHoverContent.ts and the helper implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Other providers could supply more refs, but the diff performs the same filter previously embedded in the hover and does not increase call frequency or asymptotic cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression: the extraction preserves the existing O(N) local work and adds no I/O, retention, rendering, or model creation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Load archive-nudge configuration text and accessibility help wording.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Only localized static strings change; reading configuration/help content does not trigger new computation or external work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant-size text emitted once per settings registration or accessibility-help construction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous constant work with no parallelism concerns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the text-only hunks.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance review of all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced the archive-nudge association path through reactive eligibility, normalization/deduplication, shared GitHub model acquisition, refresh/polling network calls, model lifecycle, provider history bounds, and existing global polling consumers. Also checked hover and static help/settings paths. No high-confidence actionable performance issue was introduced.
